title: Mars Climate Orbiter: planned vs. actual altitude at Mars (km)

source.name: Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board report

notes: NASA's $327.6 million Mars Climate Orbiter was lost in September 1999 after ground software produced thruster data in pound-force seconds while the navigation team's model expected newton-seconds. The spacecraft was supposed to enter orbit at roughly 226 km altitude; the investigation found it instead dropped to about 57 km, low enough for atmospheric forces to destroy it.
